request: For each independent hypothetical WordPress task, load the owning skill and relevant reference, then give the concrete implementation or release decision and validation needed. Do not mutate any product or publish anything. 1. A sensitive billing job stores its only payload in a transient, schedules the UUID, deletes the transient at handler entry, then calls a provider; the provider may timeout after accepting the request. Assess and describe the replacement contract. 2. A release action reports failure but SVN contains the intended tag. Release confirmation is enabled, nobody has confirmed, and the public ZIP still contains the prior version. The owner authorized upload only. Decide next actions, status and whether to replace the existing tag. 3. Profile a production site with unrelated checkout and session data; someone proposes deleting all transients before every timing sample. 4. Design a personal-data eraser for guest orders identified by email, including records that cannot be deleted. Specify callback inputs/outputs, batching and retry behavior. 5. A dynamic block changes attribute oldTitle to heading; ten thousand published posts will not be opened in the editor. Is switching render_callback sufficient? 6. A block editor sidebar edits registered post meta using an immediate REST POST on every keystroke; the author expects Cancel, save and reload to follow the editor's pending state. Design the appropriate ownership and test boundary. 7. A PHP pattern uses the current price while creating its markup. After insertion, its original source changes. Describe what saved pages display and the appropriate mechanism if live prices are required. 8. Assess new Plugin Directory submission eligibility for an AI tool that executes generated PHP and a renamed copy of an existing plugin. What current sources are needed, and what can be concluded about existing listings and private tools? 9. A classic theme outputs wp_head after the opening body tag, omits wp_body_open, and calls wp_footer after closing html. Specify corrections and proof. 10. A disposable staging fixture has explicit authorization to invalidate only its owned cache keys for one cold-cache test. Is that necessarily forbidden? 11. A standalone plugin admin application intentionally persists a setting immediately through REST. Must every such save be converted to editor-buffered metadata? 12. A PHP pattern is re-registered on later requests for insertion into other pages. Does saved-page persistence mean that PHP never runs again?
